text:
Situation: Ertapenem inventory is limited across both campuses. Corvale East holds 448 units at 14.9 units per day, providing 30 days on hand. Corvale General holds two lots: 470.22 units at 28.1 days and 252.5 units at 15.3 days. Combined daily use is approximately 48.1 units.

Why (FDA record): FDA inspection 955350 of ACS Dobfar S.p.A. (FEI 3006028606) ended on 2016-01-19 and was classified OAI, with the classification known on 2016-04-18. The plant was later inspected on 2017-07-21 (VAI), 2018-04-13 (VAI), 2022-04-08 (VAI), and 2024-12-13 (VAI). A Warning Letter was issued to the plant on 2017-01-13. Ertapenem is not listed on the FDA drug shortage list as of 2026-10-21.

Our position: Current supply covers roughly three to four weeks. No FDA shortage listing exists to trigger allocation programs. Alternative manufacturers are not on the FDA shortage list today, but their labels do not name a plant we could verify.

Recommended actions:
1. Buyer to contact Apotex Corp, BluePoint Laboratories, Dr.Reddys Laboratories Inc., ENDO USA, Inc., and Eugia US LLC for immediate quotes and plant disclosure; buyer approves purchase orders.
2. Buyer to request plant identification from each supplier’s regulatory affairs contact; buyer and quality assurance manager approve vendor qualification.
3. Pharmacy director to set a reorder trigger at 14 days on hand for each campus; pharmacy director approves.
4. Buyer to report weekly inventory and procurement status to P&T committee chair until supply exceeds 60 days; P&T committee chair acknowledges.

Not recommended: Switching to alternative carbapenems or changing formulary status without P&T clinical review.
